Although downwind measurements, which would serve as a benchmark, were not available, validation of the EPIcode results could be ascertained through comparison with results from other dispersion models. Those comparisons are discussed in Section 3.2.2 19 LLNL-TR-818768 The benefits of comparing real world cases with six widely-used dense gas models (e.g., TRACE, PHAST, SCIPUFF, SLAB, HG-SYSTEM, ALOHA) are that they have consistent parameters and methods and well known details such as: • Source information, weather, location • Downwind distances from 100 to 25,000 m • Peak Centerline concentration data • Maximum plume width at specific concentration levels • Developed from public sources (NTSB) We selected two actual rail car accidents (Hanna et. al, 2008) to compare against, one in Festus, Missouri in 2002, the other in Macdona, Texas during 2004.
